title: Connect an Agent: add WorkBuddy, Doubao Work and QwenWork cards, and tidy the client list
body:
domain:ui#1 · baozhoutao · session_01RKKVnjTUZ5msaYZGKf3wVv

## What

The **Connect an Agent** page (Account → Developer → Connect an Agent, and Setup → Connect an Agent; the `mcp:connect-agent` widget in `@object-ui/app-shell`) has no connect instructions for the Chinese desktop work assistants that teams here use: **WorkBuddy** (Tencent), **Doubao Work** (豆包工作) and **QwenWork** (千问办公). A user of those clients has to work out the menu path and the client's own spelling of the Streamable HTTP transport by hand.

Evidence: a product gap the maintainer requested directly. Today the page offers cards for claude.ai / Claude Desktop, Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code / Copilot and Codex CLI only, so no card names where WorkBuddy, Doubao Work or QwenWork take a custom MCP server or how each spells the transport.

## Scope (as agreed with the maintainer)

- Add cards for WorkBuddy (the `mcpServers` entry with `type: "streamableHttp"`, and the Trust step), Doubao Work (the name / transport / URL its custom-connector form asks for) and QwenWork (the `mcpServers` JSON with `type: "streamable-http"`). Each names the `Authorization: Bearer <API key>` fallback for a client version without the browser sign-in.
- Order: international clients first, then the Chinese ones. One list, no group headings.
- Merge the claude.ai / Claude Desktop and Claude Code cards into one full-width Claude card.
- Turn the Codex CLI card into a Codex card for the Codex app's MCP form (Settings → MCP servers → Add server), and list it ahead of Cursor.
- Drop the VS Code / Copilot card.
- Title the Doubao Work and QwenWork cards from the locale pack, so zh shows 豆包工作 and 千问办公.
- Reveal a minted key in the `Authorization: Bearer` form as well as `x-api-key`; wrap long one-line snippets instead of clipping them.
- All strings in the ten built-in packs; update `content/docs/ai/connect-mcp.mdx`.

## Not in scope

- Nothing on the server: the MCP endpoint, OAuth and API-key handling are unchanged (`Authorization: Bearer <key>` is already accepted).
- DuMate was considered and dropped by the maintainer.

## Open question for verification

The menu paths and transport spellings come from the vendors' docs and third-party guides read through search; they were not checked against a live install of each client.
